Film #1 — THE SHADOW (brain pick: topic FEAR, ~150 s)
Why FEAR: universal, not on Day One’s list nor ours, native to a dark world, with a physical spine device. Hero for this film: the bone-white figure (the villain is his own shadow). Shadow = homothety about the lamp, k = (1 − z_lamp)/(z_hero − z_lamp), feet anchored on the wall/floor junction; readout = 1.8 m · k. Walking toward the wall shrinks it; at the wall k = 1 → exactly his size.
Beats: 01 Every night, it was there (8.0 m) · 02 The corner + red lines stay. / not yet. / what if. · 03 Lights out · 04 One step (back view) · 05 The walk, shaft + dust (2.6 m) · 06 The wall — “When he touched the wall, the shadow was exactly his size.” (1.9 m) · 07 End card WALK TOWARD IT. Quotable: “Fear is a shadow. Walk toward it — and it is exactly your size.” Palette: BLACK 7·7·9 · WALL 14·14·15 · BONE 236·232·222 · SLATE 96·102·112 · AMBER 255·214·170 · RED 214·38·32.
Current state
2026-10-09 (turn 17): registered on all four platforms; look-dev v0 rendered and measured — setup frames luma 28.5–31.7, chroma 7.6–9.0, dark share 0.64–0.73, hero p99 ≈ 190; lights-out frame luma 10.8; end card 1.9. Targets for the film: luma 14–30 per setup frame, chroma ≤ 10, dark ≥ 0.6, −16.5 ± 1 LUFS, ≥3 callbacks, 2 quotable lines, title pun.

CREATIVE LOCK
Topic: The invisible queue — every day you delay, somebody else takes the seat that could have been yours.
Audience and language: Desi audience · easy Urdunglish · motivational FOMO and curiosity.
Master structure: 74.00 seconds · 34 voice-led beats · maximum beat 4.70 seconds.
Format: 1920×1080 · 16:9 landscape · 24 fps.
Shared performance: selected voice-00, used exactly and never time-stretched.


WF-03 EXECUTION
A new rain-soaked midnight railway platform with the humanised Monarch, controlled cyan fluorescent pools, red warning accents, practical reflections, breath and rain, a self-punching ticket, departure-board time, train occlusion, and the reserved yellow seat as the satisfying reveal. It deliberately avoids THE SHADOW’s lantern/shadow device and THE WINDOW’s apartment/window device. The original 72 BPM station score and 121 synchronized rail, rain, electrical, ticket, flap, carriage, room, and transition events remain narration-first.

Picture: mean luma 26.22 · dark share 0.823 · p99 highlight 203.83 · motion floor 0.0745 · no empty samples · no perfectly still sampled pairs.

REPRODUCIBILITY AND LEARNING
The permanent package stores the exact voice master, shared script/timeline, selected DNA, deterministic renderer, procedural soundtrack builder, event ledger, measured gate suite, look sheet, failure/fix history, and delivery receipts. Promoted safeguards include: keep implemented transitions explicit in DNA; clamp fractional-power envelopes; clamp strip coordinates; smoke-test every boundary; explicitly resample loudnorm output to 48 kHz; cache environments at 6 Hz while retaining full-rate cinema motion; preserve separate workflow implementations despite shared narrative; and never infer a film number.

V2 CREATIVE REDESIGN
The rain-soaked platform and humanised Monarch remain unmistakably WF-03, but the station is rebuilt in foreground/midground/background depth. Measured platform dolly, lens breath, wet-floor reflection, foreground-column occlusion, volumetric practicals, fog parallax, three rain depths, precision shutter echoes and 12 railway-specific transitions carry the holds. Cold cyan/red tension shifts to amber only after action.


FIVE EARNED SET PIECES
1. A macro ticket printer opens into an eleven-layer mechanical Z tunnel under a red scanner.
2. Passing carriage windows become the colour-coded dopamine tunnel.
3. Thirty punched holes lift from the ticket into an amber volumetric constellation.
4. Rain freezes around “LEKIN SACH?” while the virtual camera orbits the truth card.
5. Platform lines, hole constellation and carriage windows converge through one amber door.
